chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! These two companions of mine were ignorant that they should pause at Muzdalifa.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'They should return to their places and pause at the Mash'ar for a while.' I said, 'But no one informed them until today, and the people have left.' So he (peace be upon him) lowered his head for a while, then said: 'Is it not so that both of them had prayed the morning prayer at Muzdalifa?' I said, 'Yes.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it not so that they had both performed Qunoot in their prayer?' I said, 'Yes.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Their Hajj is complete.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Mash'ar is from Muzdalifa, and Muzdalifa is from the Mash'ar. And indeed, a little supplication suffices them.'

key_terms.الْمَشْعَر: The Mash'ar, referring to the Monument (Jamarat) area, often used interchangeably with Muzdalifa in this context
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَة: Muzdalifa, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims pause after leaving Mina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who missed pausing at Muzdalifa due to ignorance?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the principle of *sahh al-hujjah* (validating the act despite minor omission) for those who missed the specific *wuquf* at Mash'ar al-Haram due to ignorance. He clarifies the geographical and ritual continuity between Muzdalifa and the Monument, ruling that the morning prayer and Qunoot performed there suffice, thereby easing the burden on pilgrims. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical flexibility (*rukhas*) in Hajj rituals when strict conditions are not met due to lack of knowledge.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! There two companions of mine who were ignorant (of the fact) that they should be pausing at Muzdalifa’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They should both go back to their places, and they should pause at the Monuments for a while’. 
I said, ‘But no one informed them until today, and the people have left’. So he<sup>asws</sup> lowered his<sup>asws</sup> head for a while, then said: ‘Is it not so that both of them had Prayed the morning (Prayer) at Al-Muzdalifa?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is it not so that they had both performed Qunoot in their Prayer?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Their Hajj is complete’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Monuments are from Al-Muzdalifa, and Al-Muzdalifa is from the Monuments. But rather, a little from the supplication would suffice them’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, these two of my friends due to ignorance have not stayed in al-Muzdalifah. He (the Imam) said, ‘They must go back to stay in al-Mash‘ar for an hour . 5 I then said that no one told them about it until today and people have already left. He (the Imam) then looked down for a while and said, ‘Did they perform the morning Salat (prayer) in al-Muzdalifah . 5 I said, ‘Yes, they did . 5 He (the Imam) asked, ‘Did they say Qunut (supplication after recitation in second Rak’at) in their Salat (prayer )? 5 I replied, ‘Yes, they did . 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘Their Hajj then is complete . 5 He (the Imam) then said, ‘Al- Mash’ar is of al-Muzdalifah and al-Muzdalifah is from al-Mash‘ar; only a little prayer is sufficient for them . ‘“
